newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks seen up on president anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks seen up on president anniversary.

text.p: Taiwan share prices are expected to rise on Tuesday, the first anniversary of President Lee Teng-hui's inauguration, as analysts and local media widely expect state-linked funds to support the market.
On Monday, the index finished down 33.58 points or 0.41 percent to 8,107.54. A 8,100-8,200 range was seen for Tuesday.
"The index likely will rise, or at least will not fall, on President Lee's inauguration anniversary," said Allen Huang of National Securities.
"Investors, especially conglomerates and institutions, will not sell shares today even if may they intend to do so (later)."

Hopes that the government would orchestrate a full-fledged rally for the inauguration anniversary had evaporated gradually ahead of Tuesday as Taiwan's top securities watchdog flatly denied lawmakers' charges that the government would engineer such a politically motivated rally.
But brokers said reports that the securities watchdog would check which securities trust funds were dumping shares on Tuesday should make institutional investors cautious about selling.
